protocol.py: 3 biology problems (2 warnings, 1 note).

1. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: A pipette too small to mix tube A4 in slot 3: 20 ul at most in
181.8 ul
   line 66:  p20.aspirate(vol, src)
   reached through: run:83 > transfer_with_appropriate_pipette:66
   At line 66 the tip mixes tube A4 in slot 3 with 1 stroke of 13.2 ul in a well holding
   181.8 ul. The P20 can draw at most 20 ul, under a fifth of the well: no stroke it can
   make will mix this well, however many times. Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well.
   Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty
   gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a
   dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: tube A4 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix with a bigger pipette (a P300 for this well): at least 5 strokes of 145.4 ul,
   `mix(5, 145.4, well)`.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [5b5eaa993f6f]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase + sample
5
   line 67:  p20.dispense(vol, dst)
   reached through: run:83 > transfer_with_appropriate_pipette:67
   At line 67 the robot put polymerase + sample 5 into tube A4 in slot 3. Take tube A4 in
   slot 3: at that moment it held 162 ul, only 132 ul of it water or buffer, and the water
   came afterwards, at line 67, to make the 270.6 ul of water or buffer the reaction is
   built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a
   reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution.
   Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a
   restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts
   on mis-primed template.
   Affected: tube A4 in slot 3.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to tube A4 in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then polymerase + sample 5 last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one
   tube, mix it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [0e26d8c2c33c]

3. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 9 wells never mixed after sample 2, sample 3, sample 4, sample 6 and
5 more went in (8% of the well)
   line 105:  p20.dispense(2, dest_well)
   At line 105 the robot added sample 2, sample 3, sample 4, sample 6 and 5 more to wells
   A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A10, A11 and 1 more in slot 4, which already held rev primer,
   buffer + sample 1, polymerase + sample 5, fwd primer + sample 9 and 1 more (this line did
   it 9 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the
   run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their
   own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is
   usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A10, A11 and 1 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A10, A11 and 1 more in slot 4 after line 105:
   `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [74d01dd20ff8]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A pipette too small to mix tube A4 in slot 3: 20 ul at most in 181.8 ul
findings.explanation: At line 66 the tip mixes tube A4 in slot 3 with 1 stroke of 13.2 ul in a well holding 181.8 ul. The P20 can draw at most 20 ul, under a fifth of the well: no stroke it can make will mix this well, however many times. Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix with a bigger pipette (a P300 for this well): at least 5 strokes of 145.4 ul, `mix(5, 145.4, well)`.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase + sample 5
findings.explanation: At line 67 the robot put polymerase + sample 5 into tube A4 in slot 3. Take tube A4 in slot 3: at that moment it held 162 ul, only 132 ul of it water or buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 67, to make the 270.6 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to tube A4 in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample, then polymerase + sample 5 last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: 9 wells never mixed after sample 2, sample 3, sample 4, sample 6 and 5 more went in (8% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 105 the robot added sample 2, sample 3, sample 4, sample 6 and 5 more to wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A10, A11 and 1 more in slot 4, which already held rev primer, buffer + sample 1, polymerase + sample 5, fwd primer + sample 9 and 1 more (this line did it 9 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A10, A11 and 1 more in slot 4 after line 105: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
